title: Wings
notes: Dense, law-positive kanaph threading from the bleeding woman through tzitzit, Malachi’s wings, the ark, Ruth, the torn skirt, and the earth’s corners is the chapter’s clear strength; symbol links and scripture placement stay clean and assertive. Residual defects are presenter staging (Notice, Mark, Read it, Be precise) and multiple author-prose sentences that open with And or That. The count “one hundred and eight” should be digits per house style. No doctrine rewrites, quote-text changes, or modern-metaphor fights are needed; the voice and density hold once the staging and sentence-open violations are cut.

This chunk tightly joins kanaph to pe’ah and the remnant edge with clean law-positive density and a useful closing tool for the reader. The symbolic assembly from garment to field to Ruth lands with force. Three author-prose sentences open with banned That/And, and one long summary sentence breaks parallel structure on the covenant clause. No doctrine or quote wording needs touch; the rest of the register and markup hold.

proposals.old: Notice how well the command itself hides in English: here the kanaph is __“borders,”__ and when the command is repeated — __“thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four *quarters* of thy vesture”__ (Deuteronomy 22:12) — it is __“quarters.”__
proposals.new: The command itself hides in English: here the kanaph is __“borders,”__ and when the command is repeated — __“thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four *quarters* of thy vesture”__ (Deuteronomy 22:12) — it is __“quarters.”__
proposals.rationale: House style forbids presenter staging such as Notice. Assert the English scatter directly.

proposals.old: That is the signal to carry through Scripture: the kanaph is where the *reminder* of the commandments is bound — the fringe is a memory-device, not the law itself — so the kanaph in a verse is a flag that the verse may be speaking of remembering — or forgetting — the commands.
proposals.new: This is the signal to carry through Scripture: the kanaph is where the *reminder* of the commandments is bound — the fringe is a memory-device, not the law itself — so the kanaph in a verse is a flag that the verse may be speaking of remembering — or forgetting — the commands.
proposals.summary: Author prose must not open with That.
proposals.rationale: House style bans sentences in author prose that start with That/And/But. “This” keeps the claim intact.

proposals.old: Be precise about what __“remember”__ asks, for in Scripture remembering is not recalling; it is *doing*.
proposals.new: In Scripture, remembering is not recalling; it is *doing*.
proposals.summary: Drop instructional staging; assert the definition.
proposals.rationale: “Be precise about” is a director cue. The definition stands stronger as a direct claim.

proposals.old: Read it beside the fringe-command and the two verses answer each other: the tzitzit were tied at the corner __“that ye may *look upon it*, and remember,”__ and restoration is promised in the same grammar — eyes that __“*see* thy teachers”__ again, and ears that hear __“this is the way.”__
proposals.new: Beside the fringe-command, the two verses answer each other: the tzitzit were tied at the corner __“that ye may *look upon it*, and remember,”__ and restoration is promised in the same grammar — eyes that __“*see* thy teachers”__ again, and ears that hear __“this is the way.”__
proposals.rationale: House style forbids staging of the Read-that family. Lead with the comparison itself.

proposals.old: And the pattern was set at Sinai: the cherubim stretch their wings __“covering the mercy seat”__ (Exodus 25:20), the testimony — the tablets of the law — goes _inside_ the ark beneath (Exodus 25:21), and God tells Moses where He will speak from:
proposals.new: The pattern was set at Sinai: the cherubim stretch their wings __“covering the mercy seat”__ (Exodus 25:20), the testimony — the tablets of the law — goes _inside_ the ark beneath (Exodus 25:21), and God tells Moses where He will speak from:
proposals.summary: Author prose must not open with And.
proposals.rationale: House style bans And-starts in author sentences. Dropping the conjunction preserves the claim and density.

proposals.old: And the psalm that promises refuge names what the covering is made of: __“under his wings shalt thou trust: his sym:sym-truth[truth] shall be thy shield and buckler”__ (Psalm 91:4) — and the truth, this book has shown, is the law.
proposals.new: The psalm that promises refuge names what the covering is made of: __“under his wings shalt thou trust: his sym:sym-truth[truth] shall be thy shield and buckler”__ (Psalm 91:4) — and the truth, this book has shown, is the law.
proposals.summary: Author prose must not open with And.
proposals.rationale: House style bans And-starts in author sentences. The assertion remains unchanged.

proposals.old: Mark where that lament sits: the same chapter opened with the enlarged fringes of the Pharisees (Matthew 23:5) — Matthew 23 begins with the kanaph counterfeited and ends with the kanaph refused.
proposals.new: The lament sits in the same chapter that opened with the enlarged fringes of the Pharisees (Matthew 23:5) — Matthew 23 begins with the kanaph counterfeited and ends with the kanaph refused.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Mark-that staging. Assert the chapter placement directly.

proposals.old: And when almost everything is judged, the kanaph is where the sym:sym-remnant[remnant] rides out the fire: __“Thou shalt also take thereof a *few in number*, and *bind them in thy skirts*”__ (Ezekiel 5:3).
proposals.new: When almost everything is judged, the kanaph is where the sym:sym-remnant[remnant] rides out the fire: __“Thou shalt also take thereof a *few in number*, and *bind them in thy skirts*”__ (Ezekiel 5:3).
proposals.summary: Author prose must not open with And.
proposals.rationale: House style bans And-starts in author sentences. The remnant claim is unchanged.

proposals.old: That is the symbol working as it always does: by structure, not by spelling.
proposals.new: The symbol works as it always does: by structure, not by spelling.
proposals.summary: Remove banned sentence-initial That in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with That. The rewrite keeps the identical claim and density.

proposals.summary: Remove banned sentence-initial And before the Leviticus quote.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with And. The colon and lead-in to the quote remain intact.

proposals.old: The law is sewn into the kanaph, and there is healing in it; the ark of the covenant sits beneath it; the covenant is made by spreading it and read in what it carries; the kingdom tears when it tears; the dispersed wait at the earth’s four corners, and the poor glean at the field’s.
proposals.new: The law is sewn into the kanaph, and there is healing in it; the ark of the covenant sits beneath it; the covenant is made by spreading it and is read in what it carries; the kingdom tears when it tears; the dispersed wait at the earth’s four corners, and the poor glean at the field’s.
proposals.summary: Restore parallel verb structure with is read.
proposals.rationale: The original drops the copula, breaking the series of is-clauses. Adding is restores grammar without changing meaning.

proposals.old: And the stranger, the fatherless, the widow who glean the corner are the next symbols to define — and after them, the remnant they add up to.
proposals.new: The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow who glean the corner are the next symbols to define — and after them, the remnant they add up to.
proposals.summary: Remove banned sentence-initial And and complete the list.
proposals.rationale: Author prose cannot start with And. Inserting and before widow also repairs the incomplete series while preserving the forward pointer.
